title: Blocked tear duct: watery or crusty eye
summary: One watery eye with mild crusting is common and often clears on its own.
whatsNormal:
Many newborns have a blocked tear duct (nasolacrimal duct) on one or both sides.

• Watery eye or dried crust in the inner corner after sleep
• Usually starts in the first weeks of life
• White or clear discharge, not thick green pus alone
• Often improves by 6–12 months as the duct opens

Gentle massage as your pediatrician shows and wiping crusts with a clean warm cloth can help.
watchFor: Increasing redness of the white part of the eye
Thick yellow-green discharge that returns quickly after cleaning
Baby rubbing eye constantly or seeming in pain
callDoctorIf: Redness spreading, swollen eyelid, or fever with eye symptoms
Eye looks cloudy or baby avoids light
Not improved by 12 months, specialist evaluation may be needed
You were given antibiotic drops, use as directed and call if worse
